\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Approximate \AtlasInlineMath{y^\star=h(A)b}, with the matrix function defined through real-symmetric spectral calculus.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
Assume \AtlasInlineMath{A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}} with spectrum in \AtlasInlineMath{[a,\beta]}, \AtlasInlineMath{a\le\beta}, and the specified \AtlasInlineMath{\beta>0}. The public function \AtlasInlineMath{h:[a,\beta]\to\mathbb{R}} is continuous, with \AtlasInlineMath{b\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
The information \AtlasInlineMath{d,a,\beta,h,b,\varepsilon} is public and \AtlasInlineMath{A} is hidden. The only hidden-data interface returns exact \AtlasInlineMath{Av} for any \AtlasInlineMath{v\in\mathbb{R}^d}. Scalar-function evaluation and polynomial-coefficient manipulation for the public function are uncharged internal computations; they do not reveal additional \AtlasInlineMath{h(A)b}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return any \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}, without restriction to a Krylov subspace and without an additional certificate.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{\|\widehat{y}-h(A)b\|_2/\|b\|_2}, and success requires it to be at most \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}. Continuity on the compact interval ensures that \AtlasInlineMath{h(A)} is finite.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Count right products with single vectors only: \AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}. A block of width \AtlasInlineMath{q} costs \AtlasInlineMath{q} calls.

The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.

The algorithm is selected using only public inputs. For every admissible input fixed before its private seed is generated, the success event has probability at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3} over that private randomness.

\textbf{Budget convention.} A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{d}: The order of the square input matrix and the dimension of each query vector. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}}

\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_{\min}(A)\ge a}

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta}: The right endpoint of the public spectral interval, with $\beta$ > 0 retained. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\beta>0,\ \beta\ge a}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_{\max}(A)\le\beta}

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Function-action error tolerance scaled by the Euclidean norm of the supplied vector. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\widehat y-h(A)b\|_2\le\varepsilon\|b\|_2}

\AtlasInlineMath{r_h(\varepsilon)}: Minimum nonnegative polynomial degree giving uniform error epsilon on the public spectral interval \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{r_h(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb N_0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{r_h(\varepsilon)=\min\{r\in\mathbb N_0:\inf_{q\in\mathbb R[z],\,\deg q\le r}\max_{z\in[a,\beta]}|h(z)-q(z)|\le\varepsilon\}}

\AtlasInlineMath{A}: The hidden real symmetric input matrix. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^{d\times d}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{b}: The public nonzero action vector. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{h(A)b}: The target matrix-function action. \textbf{Domain:} Defined by the input's spectral decomposition.

\AtlasInlineMath{A=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)U^{\mathsf T}\ \Longrightarrow\ h(A)b=U\operatorname{diag}(h(\lambda_i))U^{\mathsf T}b}

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat y}: Approximate matrix-function action vector returned by the algorithm \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\deg q\le r}

\AtlasInlineMath{t}: The maximum number of exact Lanczos calls. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb N}.

\AtlasInlineMath{t=1+r_h(\varepsilon/2)}

\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_i(A)}: Eigenvalues of a real symmetric or Hermitian matrix in nonincreasing order. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{1\le i\le d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_1(A)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d(A)}

\AtlasInlineMath{\|z\|_2}: Euclidean norm of a vector \textbf{Domain:} Finite-dimensional real or complex vector.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|z\|_2=(\sum_i|z_i|^2)^{1/2}}

\AtlasInlineMath{\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}}: The matrix operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm. \textbf{Domain:} Any compatible matrix.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\max_{\|z\|_2=1}\|Mz\|_2=\sigma_1(M)}

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta}: Upper, lower, and two-sided bounds up to constants in the same applicable regime \textbf{Domain:} Hidden constants have only the parameter dependence explicitly permitted by the associated bound.

\AtlasInlineMath{N,N_{\mathrm r}}: Single-vector query budget for exact right products Av. A block is charged by its column count. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb N_0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}

\AtlasInlineMath{N^\star}: Minimum worst-case query budget attaining this profile's success guarantee \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb N_0\cup\{+\infty\}}.

The quantity is \AtlasInlineMath{N^\star=\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{I,\omega}N_{\mathcal A}(I,\omega)}, where the infimum ranges over admissible algorithms satisfying this profile's success guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A,I,\omega}: The algorithm, fixed admissible input, and private algorithmic seed. \textbf{Domain:} Quantifiers for worst-case input and execution cost. Success probability is taken over $\omega$.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{4. Bounds and supporting evidence}
The following conditions apply to every bound in this profile, in addition to each bound's stated region and algorithm scope.

\textbf{Oracle mapping.} Only exact Av products are available; h and b are public. Scalar h evaluations and functions of known compressed matrices do not count as matrix-vector products. Neither h(A)v nor a shifted inverse is an oracle primitive.

\textbf{Guarantee mapping.} The three verified upper bounds are deterministic exact-arithmetic algorithms and satisfy the required success probability of at least 2/3. No randomized lower bound follows from this.

\textbf{Output mapping.} Return y\_hat $\in$ R\textasciicircum{}d satisfying ‖y\_hat - h(A)b‖$_2$ $\le$ $\varepsilon$‖b‖$_2$. The known function h and spectral interval remain part of the specification.

\textbf{Resource mapping.} Count only right multiplication by a single vector, \AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}. A block product of width \AtlasInlineMath{q} costs \AtlasInlineMath{q} calls. The worst-case cap holds for every input and random seed; it is not an expected call count. Reading public inputs and exact internal arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged. This budget does not certify running time or bit complexity.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{5. Local arguments}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A1 - Deterministic evaluation of the best uniform polynomial approximation.}
\textbf{Scope.} All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

By the definition of r\_h(epsilon), choose a public polynomial p of degree r\_h(epsilon) with max\_\{lambda in [a,b]\}|p(lambda)-h(lambda)|<=epsilon. The spectral theorem gives ||p(A)b-h(A)b||\_2<=epsilon||b||\_2. Horner evaluation of p(A)b uses at most r\_h(epsilon) exact matrix-vector products. All coefficients and scalar computations depend only on public h and the public spectral interval.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A2 - Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task}
\textbf{Scope.} All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

Recover \AtlasInlineMath{A} using \AtlasInlineMath{d} standard basis queries. Exact internal spectral decomposition and the public scalar function \AtlasInlineMath{h} determine \AtlasInlineMath{h(A)b}. The vector error is zero. This uses only the admitted exact-real internal computation and adds no matrix-function oracle.
